newsitem.title: UK: No casualties in attack on N.Ireland police patrol.
newsitem.headline: No casualties in attack on N.Ireland police patrol.

text.p: A Northern Ireland police patrol escaped injury in a suspected IRA bomb attack on Wednesday night in the town of Dungannon, about 40 miles (60 km) west of Belfast, police said on Thursday.
"At about 11.10 p.m. (2310 GMT) a police patrol was travelling along a road when some sort of device exploded. The vehicle was not hit and there are no injuries," a police spokeswoman told Reuters.
Security sources said bomb disposal experts would move in at first light to examine the scene.

They said the bombing bore the hallmarks of Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas who have launched a series of attacks on security patrols in the past few weeks in an intensification of a 28-year campaign to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
Britain says the IRA must declare a ceasefire which is credible and not simply tactical to win its Sinn Fein political wing a seat at talks on the future of the British province.
The IRA called off a 17-month ceasefire on February 9, 1996, saying Britain had reneged on a promise of fast entry into talks for Sinn Fein.
Britain says a truce called by pro-British Loyalist guerrillas is shaky but still in force.
Police have blamed loyalists for three attacks on Catholic nationalists since December.
British and Irish ministers are due to meet in London on Thursday for their first talks of 1997.
They will discuss a range of difficulties plaguing the Northern Ireland peace process, including the growing guerrilla threat.
